conviction_note: Near non-result: the one material new fact since DMC last spoke is the September re-escalation of fuel (Brent >$100, carrier reefer surcharges from Oct 1) against a July 29 cost guide that was cut on lower fuel, which leans the guidance line negative; it is offset by an easy banana comp, a 34% EPS beat last quarter against a thin two-analyst bar, and a COO open-market buy above spot. p_up 48 on a 7.5% absolute move gives -0.3; the findings sum to -0.5, and the two agree because the evidence is close to balanced.
bar: Q3 2026 adj EPS consensus $0.46 (Benzinga, https://www.benzinga.com/quote/DMC/earnings-forecasts) vs $0.51 (Chartmill, 2 analysts, https://www.chartmill.com/stock/quote/DMC/analyst-ratings): two sources DISAGREE, so bar-dependent findings are capped small. Revenue consensus $1.16B (Benzinga) / $1.173B (Chartmill). Company guide (call 2026-07-29, per MarketBeat/Quartr summaries, not in the press release): FY2026 adjusted net sales growth 13-15%, adjusted EBITDA $230-240M reaffirmed; Del Monte Foods FY sales raised to $625M from $600M and adj EBITDA to $35M from $23M; 2026 external cost pressures cut to $45-55M from $60-70M (https://quartr.com/events/del-monte-corporation-dmc-q2-2026_3PeB6qX5). H1 adj EBITDA $130.1M (https://investorrelations.freshdelmonte.com/news/news-details/2026/Del-Monte-Corporation-Reports-Second-Quarter-Earnings-for-Fiscal-2026/default.aspx), so the guide implies H2 adj EBITDA $100-110M; Q3 2025 adj EBITDA was $58.0M and adj EPS $0.69 (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1047340/000104734025000131/october292025-earningspr.htm). print_vs_bar_pct is on EPS.
positioning_check: Short interest 2.1M shares, 4.6% of float, 5.7 days to cover as of 2026-08-19 (Equibles, https://equibles.com/stocks/DMC); earlier 1.9M / 2.5 DTC at 2026-06-30 (https://curvedtrading.com/stocks/dmc/), borrow fee ~0.4%. Not crowded, but DTC is meaningful on 396k avg daily volume. No October settlement found. Skew: skew_25d_vol_points is null in the baseline (front chain has 72 contracts of open interest, ATM spread 54% of mid), so the option market makes no usable directional statement; put/call OI 0.76. Event-implied move 7.06% is indicative only. Tape: -6.28% over 20d, -2.22% over 5d, 33% below the 52w high and 6.65% above the 52w low, so a good deal of disappointment is already in the price.

findings.finding: Fuel re-escalated after DMC last spoke: CMA CGM's 2026-09-18 notice says Brent has traded above $100/bbl since early September on renewed Hormuz/Bab el-Mandeb escalation and sets a reefer head-haul emergency fuel surcharge of $320/TEU from 2026-10-01. On 2026-07-29 DMC cut its 2026 external cost-pressure assumption to $45-55M from $60-70M, citing lower fuel, fertilizer and diesel. DMC runs its own reefer fleet and its Q2 release already flagged 'elevated commodity and supply chain costs given the uncertainty associated with the conflict in the Middle East'. The risk is that the Q4/FY cost assumption or the $230-240M EBITDA guide is walked back.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Only one print under the DMC name (Q2 2026, +3.79%, cost guide cut and Foods guide raised). Under the FDP name, Q3 2025 fell 9.78% pre-market on a banana cost squeeze (higher production, procurement and distribution costs) (https://www.itiger.com/news/1176769225).
findings.why_not_priced: The stock is -6.3% over 20 days and -33% from its high, so part of this is plausibly in the price. What is not priced is the company's own number: the $45-55M cost assumption stands unrevised, nobody covering the name has published a cut (Chartmill shows no target revisions in 1-3 months), and consensus Q3 EPS of $0.46-0.51 is below Q2's $0.72 for seasonal reasons, not because of a fuel cut. If the market had fully priced a guide cut, the stock would be at or below its 52w low ($26.47), not 6.65% above it.
findings.independence: Proxy: macro-to-company transmission that DMC has not confirmed. Dole plc's Q2 release (2026-08-10, after DMC spoke) attributes a 30.9% fall in Fresh Fruit adj EBITDA partly to higher shipping costs, but expects contractual pricing mechanisms to help in H2, which cuts the size (https://www.morningstar.com/news/business-wire/20260810083577/dole-plc-reports-second-quarter-2026-financial-results). Brent >$102 on 2026-10-02 (https://gulfnews.com/business/energy/brent-crude-oil-surges-past-102-amid-hormuz-tensions-us-iran-conflict-1.500695537).

findings.finding: Costa Rican colón strength continued through Q3: the BCCR reference was about ₡445-454/$ in September 2026 against roughly ₡497 at the start of the year. DMC's Q2 release and Dole's Q2 both cite the colón as a gross-profit headwind, because Costa Rica is the main cost base for DMC's bananas and pineapples.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: No clean isolated reaction. The colón was cited in Q2 2026 (stock +3.79% on an EPS beat), so the market has not punished this line on its own.
findings.why_not_priced: Largely priced: the company named it in July and consensus EPS is down roughly 30% y/y ($0.46-0.51 vs $0.69). What may not be in the bar is a further step-up, since the colón kept strengthening after Q2. If fully priced, estimates would have moved after July, and Chartmill shows no revisions.
findings.independence: Dole Q2 cites the colón as a Fresh Fruit headwind (https://www.morningstar.com/news/business-wire/20260810083577/dole-plc-reports-second-quarter-2026-financial-results). Tico Times on colón strength (https://ticotimes.net/2026/06/24/costa-rica-dollar-exchange-rate-may-have-hit-bottom).

findings.finding: The banana segment has an easy comparison and supportive peer pricing. Q3 2025 banana gross profit was only $4.6M (1.3% margin). DMC closed four low-profitability Costa Rican banana farms (a $10.6M Q2 charge). Dole's Q2 (2026-08-10, after DMC spoke) said underlying North American banana pricing was slightly higher and that contractual pricing mechanisms should help in H2. The offset is weak NA banana volumes, which both companies report.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: The banana margin collapse drove the -9.78% pre-market move on Q3 2025. In Q2 2026, banana GP fell to $8.4M from $30.0M y/y and the stock still rose 3.79% on the EPS beat.
findings.why_not_priced: Consensus anchors on Q2's -72% banana GP y/y; the y/y base for Q3 is roughly a fifth of Q2's. A preview that extrapolates the Q2 decline rate would set the banana bar too low. If this were priced, the y/y banana framing in previews would show a flat-to-up comparison.
findings.independence: Dole Q2 2026 release (https://www.morningstar.com/news/business-wire/20260810083577/dole-plc-reports-second-quarter-2026-financial-results). Farm closures: Q2 10-Q (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001047340/000104734026000042/fdp-20260626.htm).

findings.finding: Avocado selling prices stayed down. Mission Produce, reporting on 2026-09-08 for May-July, saw per-unit avocado prices fall 9% on higher Mexican supply, and guided industry volumes up about 10% y/y for Aug-Oct. DMC already cited lower avocado prices in its Q2 fresh and value-added segment, so the pressure persisted through DMC's Q3. Net of the rest of the company: avocados are part of the $569M F&VA segment, alongside pineapple, fresh-cut and prepared items.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q2 2026 revenue missed consensus by about 7.5% ($1.219B vs $1.318B), partly on F&VA, and the stock still rose 3.79%: this name has not been punished for revenue misses when EPS beat.
findings.why_not_priced: Mission's print came after DMC's last call. With two analysts, the revenue bar ($1.16-1.17B) may not have been refreshed for avocado pricing. If priced, the revenue consensus would sit nearer Q3 2025 adjusted sales ($960M) plus a Foods run-rate.
findings.independence: Peer print (Mission) plus DMC's own Q2 avocado commentary (https://www.freshfruitportal.com/news/2026/07/30/del-monte-q2/). These are one theme from two sources.

findings.finding: President & COO Mohammed Abbas bought 12,000 shares on the open market on 2026-08-04 at a $29.89 weighted average (about $359k), lifting his direct holding to 71,930 shares. That price is above today's $28.69 spot, and he bought six days after the Q2 print, with knowledge of July trading.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: No prior instance of this line in the record.
findings.why_not_priced: The Form 4 is public, but the stock has since fallen below his purchase price, so the market has not treated it as a floor. If priced as a signal, the stock would not trade 4% under an insider's buy price made with the first month of the quarter visible.
findings.independence: The only other Form 4 since July is an officer's small PSU-related sale of 245 shares at $32.03 on 2026-09-08 (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1047340/000176973726000009/xslF345X06/wk-form4_1788988469.xml), a weak opposite signal.

findings.finding: Seneca Foods' fiscal Q1 (April-June 2026), reported in August after DMC spoke, showed net sales up 36.2% to $405.2M, almost entirely on canned and frozen vegetable volume (about +$96.8M). That is consistent with Seneca taking share while Del Monte Foods was in bankruptcy and SKU rationalization. It is a competitive headwind for DMC's prepared foods volume.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: First quarters of the combined Foods business; only one data point (Q2 2026, Foods guide raised, stock +3.79%).
findings.why_not_priced: It is mostly priced: Seneca's quarter overlaps DMC's Q2, which DMC reported with a Foods guide raise. What remains is the possibility that share loss deepens through the Q3 pack season. Net of the rest: Foods is guided at $625M of roughly $4.8B group sales, so this lands on a minority segment.
findings.independence: Proxy (competitor). Contradicted in direction by DMC's own Foods guide raise of 2026-07-29 (https://quartr.com/events/del-monte-corporation-dmc-q2-2026_3PeB6qX5), hence the small size.

findings.finding: Last quarter's setup favours an EPS beat. Q2 2026 adj EPS was $0.72 against a $0.54 estimate (+34%), with revenue missing by 7.5%. Management then raised the Foods EBITDA guide by $12M (to $35M), cut the external cost assumption by $15M, and reaffirmed FY adj EBITDA of $230-240M. Coverage is two analysts and the Q3 bar is $0.46-0.51. Note that the bar is disputed (two sources disagree), so this finding is capped small.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: The Q2 2026 EPS beat of +34% with a revenue miss bought only +3.79%. Beats are bought, but modestly.
findings.why_not_priced: With two analysts and no target revisions in 1-3 months, the Q3 estimate may not reflect the July guide raise flowing through. If priced, the estimates would have moved up after the July raise rather than sitting at $0.46-0.51.
findings.independence: Q2 numbers are from the company release (https://investorrelations.freshdelmonte.com/news/news-details/2026/Del-Monte-Corporation-Reports-Second-Quarter-Earnings-for-Fiscal-2026/default.aspx). Benzinga carries the $0.46 bar (https://www.benzinga.com/quote/DMC/earnings-forecasts).

findings.finding: IEEPA tariffs were struck down (Supreme Court, 2026-02-20). On 2026-03-04 the CIT ordered refunds to importers of record, and CBP had processed $22B of Phase 1 refunds by June. DMC (then FDP) disclosed 'tariff-related charges in North America' in its 2025 distribution costs, and no refund recognition appeared in Q1 or Q2 2026. A refund could land in Q3 as a one-off. The amount is undisclosed, and it is not established that DMC has claimed.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: None for this name. Across the repo, tariff-refund names split by guidance direction, not by the refund.
findings.why_not_priced: Unquantified and not mentioned by the company. It is a one-off with no path to the guide, so it is sized at a fraction.
findings.independence: FDP 2025 10-Q mentions tariff-related charges (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1047340/000104734025000107/fdp-20250627.htm). The CIT order (https://fortune.com/2026/03/04/judge-orders-trump-to-pay-tariff-refunds-to-companies-court-international-trade/).

findings.finding: Costa Rican pineapple supply tightness should support DMC's pricing (DMC is the largest pineapple marketer, and pineapple pricing drove its 2025 gross-profit increase). An exporter reported on 2026-04-17 that prices stayed more than 20% higher after annual programs closed, and the sector expected a supply gap of about 12 weeks after week 30 (late July-October), which falls inside DMC's Q3. The volume loss partly offsets the price.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: FY2025 gross profit rose to $299.4M from $243.3M, mainly on pineapple pricing (FDP 10-K). The stock reaction on that specific line is not isolated.
findings.why_not_priced: Trade-press only and dated April, so partly known. A Q3-specific supply gap is not something a two-analyst consensus is likely to model. If priced, the F&VA margin bar would sit above Q2's 11.0%.
findings.independence: The +20% pricing comes from a second exporter in a separate article (https://www.freshplaza.com/article/9830170/pineapple-demand-remains-strong-but-high-prices-may-lead-some-consumers-to-look-for-alternatives/). FDP 10-K on pineapple pricing (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1047340/000104734026000015/fdp-20251226.htm).

findings.finding: On 2026-07-15 DMC upsized its revolver to $900M from $750M and removed the 10bp SOFR adjustment. At Q2 it had $413.0M drawn (up from $173.0M at year end, after the $310M Foods acquisition), the leverage covenant was raised to 4.25x for four quarters, and Q2 interest expense was $6.4M vs $3.0M. What the money buys is the seasonal pack-season inventory build of the canned vegetable business in Q3, not distress, so Q3 interest and working capital will be heavier.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: No prior reaction on this line.
findings.why_not_priced: Public 8-K and 10-Q, so mostly priced. The residual is the Q3 interest and cash-flow optics of a pack season that this company has never reported before.
findings.independence: The Q2 10-Q gives the drawn balance and covenant (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001047340/000104734026000042/fdp-20260626.htm). Same issuer; documents are distinct.

outside_window.finding: Foreign tax authorities have issued transfer-pricing deficiencies of about $275.9M including interest and penalties for 2012-2021 across three jurisdictions. The company disputes them and has accrued nothing extra. Resolution is not dated and is not expected inside the window.
